problem: Prior single-image 3D modeling is limited by render distance, field of view and depth estimators, and video generators lack physical grounding, so agents cannot explore unseen parts of a scene. Embodied policies given only one egocentric view lack visibility into unseen regions.
motivation: Humans build a mental 3D model from a glimpse and imagine unseen areas to decide. Physically exploring is costly or dangerous, so a generative, physically grounded, explorable 360-degree world could give agents informed observations without moving.
key_idea: Generate an explorable 360-degree world from a single image via image-to-panorama initialization plus action-conditioned panoramic video diffusion with spherical-consistency learning, and let an LMM agent act on imagined observations (Imagination-Augmented Policy).
insight: Spherical-consistency learning and panoramic representation matter for quality: FVD is 69.5 with SCL, 81.9 without, and 196.7 for the cubemap baseline. Text-only GPT outperforms multimodal single-view GPT, so a single view without imagination can mislead; adding imagined exploration raises GPT-4o accuracy from 46.10 to 85.22. Loop-consistency tests show minimal drift because rotations are applied on the sphere without quality loss.
method: World initialization: a FLUX.1-based text-to-panorama LoRA model extended to condition on a single image and a text description to output a 360-degree equirectangular panorama.
World transition: action a_t=(rotation angle, distance) drives panoramic video generation from the last explored panorama; the video diffusion model is conditioned on the rotated panorama plus noise.
Sphere rotation: the action's rotation is applied on the spherical representation of the equirectangular panorama with a lossless geometric transform T.
Spherical-consistency learning (SCL): a training technique for smooth, continuous imagery across all viewing directions, removing seams at panorama edges.
Data engine: cubemap exploration trajectories collected in Unreal Engine 5 and Unity, converted to equirectangular panoramas for training.
Exploration modes: interactive (human), GPT-4o-assisted free exploration to avoid collapse, and goal-driven navigation with GPT planning of low-level configurations.
Imagination-Augmented Policy: an LMM chooses action A from the initial image plus imagined observations; the multi-agent version imagines other agents' positions and views.

setting.backbone: FLUX.1-based panorama diffusion (image+text conditioned) + panoramic video diffusion model (trained); GPT-4o (frozen) as exploration pilot and embodied policy
setting.training_data: Synthetic exploration cubemap/panorama videos curated from Unreal Engine 5 and Unity (scale not given in this text); pretrained FLUX.1 panorama LoRA
setting.observation: Single RGB image, then generated egocentric 360-degree panoramas / panoramic videos
setting.action_space: Continuous (rotation angle, forward distance) exploration actions; high-level embodied actions such as answering questions or navigation plans
setting.simulator: Unreal Engine 5 and Unity for data curation; the generative world itself serves as the environment
setting.privileged: none stated (training data comes from simulators)

numbers.extra: Extends the GenEx-EQA of the earlier GenEx paper (Lu et al. 2024); imagined panoramic videos given as input
numbers.evidence: Table 'Eval of Imagination-Augmented Policy', row GPT4-o with GenEx
Table 'Evaluation of Multi-Agent Imagination-Augmented Policy', row GPT4-o with GenEx

numbers.backbone: GenEx panoramic video diffusion with SCL

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark is evaluated. Loop-consistency (IELC) results appear only in a figure.
results: GPT-4o with GenEx reaches 85.22% accuracy on single-agent EQA versus 46.10% for multimodal GPT-4o, and 94.87% on multi-agent versus 21.88%. GenEx with SCL beats the 6-view cubemap baseline on all video quality metrics (FVD 69.5 vs 196.7). Humans also improve with GenEx (94.00 vs 91.50 single-agent, 77.41 vs 55.24 multi-agent).
limitations: Relies on physics-engine synthetic data; sim-to-real adaptation, real sensor integration and dynamic conditions remain open.
Generation quality degrades over long exploration and can collapse with poor human commands such as moving too close to a wall.
Evaluation is a custom EQA-style decision benchmark and mostly qualitative demos, with no standard navigation benchmarks.
